questions.q: What was the name of the inn kept by the narrator's father?
choices: The Admiral Benbow
The Royal George
The Spy-glass
The Dead Man's Chest
questions.evidence: my father kept the Admiral Benbow inn

questions.q: What mark did the old seaman have on his face?
choices: A sabre cut across one cheek
A black patch over his left eye
A tattoo of an anchor on his chin
A burn on his forehead
questions.evidence: the sabre cut across one cheek

questions.q: What did the seaman say people might call him?
choices: Captain
Matey
Black Dog
Old Billy

questions.q: Why did the captain throw gold pieces on the threshold when he arrived?
choices: To pay in advance for his stay
To bribe the father to keep a secret
To show off to the neighbours
To pay the man who pushed his barrow
questions.evidence: You can tell me when I've worked through that

questions.q: Why did the captain choose the Admiral Benbow over the other inns on the coast?
choices: It was described as lonely
It was the cheapest inn on the coast
It had the best rum
It was the closest inn to Bristol
questions.evidence: described as lonely, had chosen it from the others

questions.q: How did the captain spend most of his days?
choices: Watching the cove and cliffs with a brass telescope
Fishing for mackerel from a small boat in the cove
Sleeping late in his room above the parlour
Walking to the village each day to buy more rum
questions.evidence: All day he hung round the cove or upon the cliffs with a brass telescope

questions.q: Why did the captain ask every day whether seafaring men had gone by?
choices: He wanted to avoid them
He missed the company of his own kind
He hoped to find a crew
He was waiting for a letter from Bristol
questions.evidence: at last we began to see he was desirous to avoid them

questions.q: What did the captain pay the narrator to watch out for?
choices: A seafaring man with one leg
A blind beggar with a stick
A ship flying a black flag in the bay
A man with two fingers missing
questions.evidence: weather-eye open for a seafaring man with one leg

questions.q: How much did the captain promise to pay the narrator each month?
choices: A silver fourpenny
A golden guinea
Three golden guineas
A silver shilling
questions.evidence: promised me a silver fourpenny on the first of every month

questions.q: How did the one-legged man affect the narrator?
choices: He haunted the narrator's dreams on stormy nights
He made the narrator long to become a sailor
He made the narrator laugh at the captain's fears
He made the narrator want to stop working at the inn
questions.evidence: How that personage haunted my dreams

questions.q: The narrator says the captain was "the most overriding companion ever known." What does "overriding" mean here?
choices: Bossy and controlling
Quiet, shy and timid
Funny and always cheerful
Generous and very kind
questions.evidence: he was the most overriding companion ever known

questions.q: Why does the narrator believe the captain's presence actually did the inn some good?
choices: He brought excitement to a quiet country life
He paid far more than any of the other guests
He scared away the thieves who robbed travellers
He helped the family with the work of the inn
questions.evidence: it was a fine excitement in a quiet country life

questions.q: What happened when the narrator's father tried to ask the captain for more money?
choices: The captain stared him out of the room
The captain paid him in full at once
The captain drew a knife on him
The captain left the inn for a week
questions.evidence: stared my poor father out of the room

questions.q: What did the captain do right after Dr. Livesey kept talking instead of falling silent?
choices: Shouted "Silence, there, between decks!"
Left the parlour and went up to bed
Bought the doctor a glass of rum
Began singing his song even louder

questions.q: How did Dr. Livesey react when the captain threatened him with a clasp-knife?
choices: He stayed calm and warned the captain he would hang
He ran out of the inn and rode off on his horse
He drew a pistol and pointed it at the captain
He called loudly for the narrator's father to help
questions.evidence: The doctor never so much as moved.

questions.q: What is this chapter mostly about?
choices: A frightening old captain moves into the inn and Dr. Livesey stands up to him
The narrator sails away with the captain to find his treasure
Pirates attack the Admiral Benbow at night and the narrator's family must flee
The narrator's father sells the Admiral Benbow and buys a bigger inn in Bristol
questions.evidence: the brown old seaman with the sabre cut first took up his lodging under our roof
